title: Proverbs, Chapter 19 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 19 on folio 416r of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 19 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folio 416r.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>טֽוֹב־רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו וְה֣וּא כְסִֽיל׃ <sup>2</sup>גַּ֤ם בְּלֹא־דַ֣עַת נֶ֣פֶשׁ לֹא־ט֑וֹב וְאָ֖ץ בְּרַגְלַ֣יִם חוֹטֵֽא׃ <sup>3</sup>אִוֶּ֣לֶת אָ֭דָם תְּסַלֵּ֣ף דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְעַל־יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִזְעַ֥ף לִבּֽוֹ׃ <sup>4</sup>ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּ יִפָּרֵֽד׃ <sup>5</sup>עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט׃ <sup>6</sup>רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי־נָדִ֑יב וְכָל־הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן׃ <sup>7</sup>כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי־רָ֨שׁ ׀ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא־ [לוֹ־] הֵֽמָּה׃ <sup>8</sup>קֹֽנֶה־לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא־טֽוֹב׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool. <sup>2</sup>Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth. <sup>3</sup>The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD. <sup>4</sup>Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour. <sup>5</sup>A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape. <sup>6</sup>Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts. <sup>7</sup>All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him. <sup>8</sup>He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֖יחַ כְּזָבִ֣ים יֹאבֵֽד׃ פ <sup>10</sup>לֹֽא־נָאוֶ֣ה לִכְסִ֣יל תַּעֲנ֑וּג אַ֝ף כִּֽי־לְעֶ֤בֶד ׀ מְשֹׁ֬ל בְּשָׂרִֽים׃ <sup>11</sup>שֵׂ֣כֶל אָ֭דָם הֶאֱרִ֣יךְ אַפּ֑וֹ וְ֝תִפאַרְתּ֗וֹ עֲבֹ֣ר עַל־פָּֽשַׁע׃ <sup>12</sup>נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל־עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃ <sup>13</sup>הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה׃ <sup>14</sup>בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת׃ <sup>15</sup>עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב׃ <sup>16</sup>שֹׁמֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ בּוֹזֵ֖ה דְרָכָ֣יו יומת [יָמֽוּת׃]
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish. <sup>10</sup>Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes. <sup>11</sup>The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and it is his glory to pass over a transgression. <sup>12</sup>The king's wrath is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour is as dew upon the grass. <sup>13</sup>A foolish son is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping. <sup>14</sup>House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from the LORD. <sup>15</sup>Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger. <sup>16</sup>He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>מַלְוֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה ח֣וֹנֵֽן דָּ֑ל וּ֝גְמֻל֗וֹ יְשַׁלֶּם־לֽוֹ׃ <sup>18</sup>יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְאֶל־הֲ֝מִית֗וֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ <sup>19</sup>גרל־ [גְּֽדָל־] חֵ֭מָה נֹ֣שֵׂא עֹ֑נֶשׁ כִּ֥י אִם־תַּ֝צִּ֗יל וְע֣וֹד תּוֹסִֽף׃ <sup>20</sup>שְׁמַ֣ע עֵ֭צָה וְקַבֵּ֣ל מוּסָ֑ר לְ֝מַ֗עַן תֶּחְכַּ֥ם בְּאַחֲרִיתֶֽךָ׃ <sup>21</sup>רַבּ֣וֹת מַחֲשָׁב֣וֹת בְּלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וַעֲצַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תָקֽוּם׃ <sup>22</sup>תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְטֽוֹב־רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב׃ <sup>23</sup>יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה לְחַיִּ֑ים וְשָׂבֵ֥עַ יָ֝לִ֗ין בַּל־יִפָּ֥קֶד רָֽע׃ <sup>24</sup>טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת גַּם־אֶל־פִּ֝֗יהוּ לֹ֣א יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again. <sup>18</sup>Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying. <sup>19</sup>A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver him, yet thou must do it again. <sup>20</sup>Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end. <sup>21</sup>There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand. <sup>22</sup>The desire of a man is his kindness: and a poor man is better than a liar. <sup>23</sup>The fear of the LORD tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil. <sup>24</sup>A slothful man hideth his hand in his bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>לֵ֣ץ תַּ֭כֶּה וּפֶ֣תִי יַעְרִ֑ם וְהוֹכִ֥יחַ לְ֝נָב֗וֹן יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃ <sup>26</sup>מְֽשַׁדֶּד־אָ֭ב יַבְרִ֣יחַ אֵ֑ם בֵּ֝֗ן מֵבִ֥ישׁ וּמַחְפִּֽיר׃ <sup>27</sup>חַֽדַל־בְּ֭נִי לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר לִ֝שְׁג֗וֹת מֵֽאִמְרֵי־דָֽעַת׃ <sup>28</sup>עֵ֣ד בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָלִ֣יץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְבַלַּע־אָֽוֶן׃ <sup>29</sup>נָכ֣וֹנוּ לַלֵּצִ֣ים שְׁפָטִ֑ים וּ֝מַהֲלֻמ֗וֹת לְגֵ֣ו כְסִילִֽים׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge. <sup>26</sup>He that wasteth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach. <sup>27</sup>Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge. <sup>28</sup>An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity. <sup>29</sup>Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.
